Dozens of nations warn of famine in Sudan

Dozens of countries, including the United States and major European powers, have issued a joint statement warning of a worrying deterioration in food security in Sudan. Published by the US State Department, the statement cites the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), which has warned of a risk of famine in the coming months, and stresses that the parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for easing civilian suffering.

The signatories called on the warring sides to remove all obstacles to humanitarian aid, urged the international community to increase funding, and asked financial institutions to adapt existing programmes to the food crisis.

Sudan's army has been fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023, after disputes over integrating their forces during a planned transition to civilian rule. In June, the UN-backed IPC reported 5.1 million people facing severe hunger, as farmers struggle to harvest amid war and a recent wave of drought.

Source: Middle East Monitor

Israel Votes: No Majority, Arab Parties Pivotal

Early results from Israel's general election of 28 October 2026 show neither major bloc reaching the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority. With more than half of ballots counted, The Times of Israel projected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc at 56 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition alliance at 49. Likud is projected as the largest single party with 27–28 seats, ahead of Eisenkot's Yashar with 21.

According to the Central Elections Committee, Palestinian-led parties have overtaken Naftali Bennett's Together alliance for third place. At an earlier stage of counting, the Joint List and Ra'am were projected to win 16 seats combined, enough to give Eisenkot's bloc 63 seats if they chose to back it.

Speaking at Likud headquarters in West Jerusalem, Netanyahu said a right-wing government must be formed and ruled out relying on Arab parties, adding that the true results were one or two days away. Al Jazeera analyst Marwan Bishara noted that Likud's tally is its lowest since 2009. All figures remain provisional.

Source: Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye
